items.title: Replaceable but Employed: Automation and the Meaning of Work
items.desc: Joshua Gans models jobs where workers value both producing useful output and knowing the output depends on their own contribution; a credible machine alternative can erode that second source of meaning even when it doesn't replace the worker. [NBER, posted 2026-08-03]

items.title: Predictive Risk Scores in the Public Sector: Experimental Evidence from Child-Protection Investigations
items.desc: A randomized evaluation of 4,752 child-protection referrals finds that giving supervisors an algorithmic risk score raised placements and services for the highest-risk children and cut later maltreatment referrals, with no evidence of widened racial disparities. [NBER, posted 2026-08-03]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: What Are Companies Getting for All That A.I. Spending?
items.desc: A new field of 'tokenomics' is emerging to measure the return on corporate AI spending, as executives swing from maximizing token usage to reining in the millions of dollars in compute costs it generates. [NYT, 2026-08-03]

items.title: This Is Not the Way to Hold A.I. Companies Accountable
items.desc: The NYT editorial board argues against Sam Altman's proposal that the federal government take small equity stakes (reportedly ~5%, worth about $42.6B at OpenAI) in leading AI firms so the public can share in the industry's gains. [NYT, 2026-08-03]

items.title: Can America Retrain Workers Before AI Leaves Them Behind?
items.desc: The Economist examines whether U.S. workforce-retraining efforts can keep pace as AI reshapes the labor market and threatens to displace workers faster than they can reskill. [Economist, 2026-08-02]
